Arrays and data science

NumPy and pandas make Python the default for numeric and data work. Guion now has native arrays and a first-party data-frame library, frames, but both are young. In the project's reports on one Apple M1 Pro, frames finishes five tested CSV workloads before pandas does from start to finish, mostly because pandas takes about 0.27 s to load. On compute alone, against pandas 3.1.1 and NumPy 2.5.4 and with a development build made after 0.9.0, Guion is ahead on four tests: reading a 1,000,000-row CSV takes 0.75 times what pandas takes (for repeated reads in one process; the first read in a process measured 0.97), element-wise maths 0.77 times what NumPy takes, summing 0.83 times, and sorting a million numbers 0.66 times. Matrix multiplication is about 2 times NumPy's, on Apple silicon, where NumPy uses Apple's own BLAS.

Earlier tests that reached NumPy through Python are retired and no longer cited. These figures are from the 25 November speed report, one run of each test on one machine, on a development build made after 0.9.0 (evaluation/completion/results/2026-11-25-speed-report.md in the repository).
